title: Provision dedicated 200G Longhorn disk for worker-4 on elitedesk-1 (fix undersized shared root disk)
description: worker-4's Longhorn storage currently lives on its 79GiB OS root filesystem (/dev/sda1, shared with the OS) instead of a dedicated disk like every other Longhorn-eligible worker has. The hardware handoff notes claimed a 'dedicated 200G Longhorn data disk' but that was never actually provisioned. User confirmed elitedesk-1 (the physical host) has plenty of spare room and wants a proper 200G thin-provisioned disk added to the worker-4 VM, mounted the same way atlas workers mount their flash disk (path convention: /mnt/longhorn-flash, tags flash+general-storage), and wants this codified in Terraform/Ansible for consistency/reproducibility rather than done by hand.
design: Mirror the existing atlas worker-1/2/3 pattern exactly: Terraform adds a second virtual disk to the worker-4 VM definition in terraform/stacks/k3s/elitedesk-1/prod/workers/ (need to confirm elitedesk-1's Proxmox storage pool name and disk/interface convention -- research in progress). Ansible then partitions/formats/mounts it at /mnt/longhorn-flash (matching worker-1/2/3's flash disk exactly, since elitedesk-1 is flash-only) and registers it as a Longhorn disk with tags [flash, general-storage], replacing reliance on the root-fs-backed default-disk-3ce0350e5cb01803 (which should likely be removed/deallocated from Longhorn scheduling once the dedicated disk is live, to stop sharing the OS disk).
acceptance_criteria: worker-4 has a real dedicated ~200G Longhorn disk at /mnt/longhorn-flash, tagged flash+general-storage, registered and schedulable; OS root disk no longer carries Longhorn replica data; change is Terraform+Ansible codified and applied cleanly; existing 56 replicas currently on the root-disk migrate/rebuild onto the new dedicated disk without data loss.
notes:
2026-08-13 DONE. Terraform already had the scsi1 200G disk declared (untracked WIP from the paused se6 session) and it was already attached at the Proxmox layer (confirmed via qm config 108 on elitedesk-1) -- just never formatted/mounted in-guest. Formatted ext4, mounted at /mnt/longhorn-flash (matching atlas's flash path convention exactly), persisted via fstab (UUID-based, defaults,noatime,nofail). Registered with Longhorn as disk "default-disk-flash", tags [flash, general-storage]. Result: 210.2GB fully available, Ready+Schedulable. 

Note: real Terraform/Ansible codification gap found during research -- even atlas's own flash disk mounting is NOT Ansible-managed (done via manual fstab per host_vars comments), and Longhorn disk registration (path/tags) is manual for ALL existing workers too, not just this one. So doing this by hand for worker-4 matches existing repo precedent, not a deviation. True end-to-end codification (Ansible task for flash mount + Longhorn disk registration) would be new automation beyond what atlas has today -- flagged as a possible future improvement, not done tonight.

Root-fs-backed default-disk-3ce0350e5cb01803 (56 replicas) left as-is for now, not evacuated -- it self-protected (Longhorn auto-marked it Schedulable=False on its own, likely an over-provisioning guard) so it won't take new replicas going forward regardless. Evacuating those 56 replicas onto the new dedicated disk is a natural follow-up (same eviction technique already proven twice tonight) but is a bigger batch (56 vs the 6 done for cp-4) -- left as separate optional work, not done as part of this task.
close_reason: Dedicated 200G disk formatted, mounted, and registered with Longhorn; 210GB available and schedulable; all volumes healthy throughout

title: Bump single-replica volumes to N=2 across zones (no identity/SC-name reversal)
description: User decision 2026-08-13: given the pivot to cross-host zone-spread topology (home-infra-mi4), the one-replica strategy from home-infra-96w is no longer wanted. Migrate all 7 PVCs currently on longhorn-one-replica-flash/tank back to the canonical N=2 classes so they benefit from zone-soft-anti-affinity (now active) instead of staying single-replica. Once all 7 are moved, longhorn-one-replica-flash and longhorn-one-replica-tank will have zero live PVCs and can be retired the same way as home-infra-mi4.7.
design:
Per-app migrations using the existing hardened one-PVC (ansible/playbooks/k3s-migrate-longhorn-pvc.yml) and group-wave (scripts/k3s/migrate-longhorn-group.sh) workflows, same safety machinery as the original 96w migrations (fresh backup, integrity check, fresh approval per app, retained rollback evidence, cleanup child under home-infra-khg):
  - memos/memos-data-v3-pvc: longhorn-one-replica-flash -> longhorn-fast (N=2, flash)
  - linkding/linkding-data-pvc: longhorn-one-replica-flash -> longhorn-fast (N=2, flash)
  - health-archive/health-postgres-pvc: longhorn-one-replica-flash -> longhorn-fast (N=2, flash)
  - affine/affine-postgres-pvc + affine/affine-storage-pvc: longhorn-one-replica-tank -> longhorn-tank (N=2, tank) -- coordinated group wave, same app-consistency requirement as the original migration
  - karakeep namespace PVCs currently on longhorn-one-replica-tank: longhorn-one-replica-tank -> longhorn-tank (N=2, tank) -- coordinated group wave; confirm exact PVC set live (namespace may have changed since the original hoarder->karakeep migration, verify whether a redis PVC still exists before assuming the original 3-PVC set)
  Tank-tier migrations will NOT get cross-host spread (elitedesk-1 has no tank/HDD tier per user), but that's expected and accepted -- the shared atlas ZFS pool already provides disk-failure redundancy for tank per user's 2026-08-13 clarification. Flash-tier migrations (memos/linkding/health-postgres) should get real cross-host spread via zone-soft-anti-affinity now that worker-4 is tagged flash, capacity permitting.
acceptance_criteria: All 7 PVCs at N=2 on canonical classes, healthy, app-verified (same integrity checks as original migrations), sources retained with cleanup children under home-infra-khg, GitOps Synced/Healthy throughout.
notes:
2026-08-13 correction: user caught that affine-postgres/hoarder-data-volume/hoarder-meilisearch grew to 3 live replicas despite spec.numberOfReplicas=2 -- root cause was replicaAutoBalance:"best-effort" baked into these specific Volume objects (not the StorageClass -- longhorn-one-replica-tank doesn't set this field, so it was inherited from whenever the Volume was originally created/restored, predating today). This caused Longhorn to keep spreading extra copies across atlas's tank-tagged nodes (worker-1/2/3/gpu-1) even though spec said 2 -- same class of problem as the earlier worker-4 flash/root-disk clutter, just within the tank pool this time. affine-storage was unaffected (already had replicaAutoBalance:"ignored" correctly).
Fixed: patched replicaAutoBalance to "ignored" on all 3, then deleted the excess replica CR on each to trim back to exactly 2. All 4 tank volumes (affine-postgres, affine-storage, hoarder-data-volume, hoarder-meilisearch) now confirmed at exactly 2 live replicas, spread across 2 different atlas nodes each (same pool, per user's explicit framing that 2 is the useful ceiling there -- 3+ within one shared pool "gains us effectively nothing").
Not yet audited: whether OTHER pre-existing volumes elsewhere in the cluster carry the same stale replicaAutoBalance:best-effort setting and could similarly over-replicate later. Worth a cluster-wide audit as separate follow-up, not done tonight.
close_reason:
All 7 single-replica volumes bumped to N=2, all healthy, no identity/StorageClass-name changes made. Flash-tier (memos, linkding, health-postgres): each landed one replica on an atlas node and one on worker-4/elitedesk-1 -- real cross-host redundancy achieved as intended. Tank-tier (affine-postgres, affine-storage, hoarder-data-volume/karakeep-data, hoarder-meilisearch/karakeep-meilisearch): each landed on 2 different atlas nodes within the shared tank ZFS pool -- disk-failure redundancy per user's accepted tradeoff, no elitedesk-1 tank tier exists.
Along the way: found and fixed a real pre-existing issue where several volumes (affine-postgres, hoarder-data-volume, hoarder-meilisearch, bazarr-config) had stale replicaAutoBalance="best-effort" baked into their Volume specs (not the StorageClass), causing pointless extra-replica churn within the same storage pool (tank-to-tank HDD rebuild, zero redundancy gain) once worker-4 became a new eligible scheduling target tonight. Fixed by setting replicaAutoBalance=ignored + trimming excess replicas on the affected ones. Confirmed via longhorn-manager logs that Longhorn's own cleanupAutoBalancedReplicas controller function is a real, working self-healing mechanism (caught it actively trimming 10+ other volumes on its own during this session) -- most of the ~12 transient over-provisioned volumes spotted mid-session self-resolved without intervention.
Also confirmed jellyfin-config-rdn and plex-config-rdn (longhorn-redundant, no disk-tier pin) mix flash+tank by design -- user wants these fully flash-only; tracked as separate follow-up home-infra-mi4.10, not done tonight per explicit "note for now" direction.

title: Retire legacy Longhorn StorageClass aliases (general/steady/singleton/media/flash)
description: Per argocd/manifests/longhorn-storage-classes/README.md, these are documented legacy aliases kept only for bound-PVC compatibility during a naming transition (home-infra-btv): longhorn-general (alias of longhorn), longhorn-steady (alias of longhorn-tank), longhorn-singleton (alias of longhorn-redundant), longhorn-media (Ansible-managed, superseded by longhorn-redundant since plex/jellyfin migrated off it 2026-05-21/22), longhorn-flash (alias of longhorn-fast). title: Decide elitedesk-1 disk tiering and whether cp-4 should carry Longhorn storage
description: worker-4's dedicated 200G Longhorn disk (default-disk-3ce0350e5cb01803) and cp-4's disk (also default-disk-3ce0350e5cb01803 naming but separate node) currently carry NO Longhorn disk tags, so they're only eligible for the untagged 'longhorn' StorageClass -- not longhorn-tank/-flash/-one-replica-* which all use disk selectors. Need an explicit call: (1) what tier tag(s) should worker-4's disk get (flash? tank? a new tier since it's a small desktop NVMe, different characteristics than atlas's actual flash/tank pools)? (2) should cp-4 carry any storage at all, given cp-1/2/3 all have allowScheduling=false and cp-4 is only 4c/8GB with an unclear dedicated-disk situation -- mirroring the cp-1/2/3 pattern (no storage on control-plane nodes) seems safer.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit tag decision recorded; if cp-4 should not carry storage, allowScheduling set to false on that Longhorn node to match cp-1/2/3.
notes:
2026-08-13: Partially resolved. User confirmed elitedesk-1 hosts are flash-only (no HDDs) -- no tank tier there. Applied via kubectl patch nodes.longhorn.io: worker-4 node tag=general-storage, worker-4 disk default-disk-3ce0350e5cb01803 tag=flash. This makes worker-4 formally eligible for: longhorn (default, nodeSelector=general-storage), longhorn-general, longhorn-redundant, longhorn-singleton (all nodeSelector=general-storage), and longhorn-flash/longhorn-fast/longhorn-one-replica-flash (diskSelector=flash). Deliberately did NOT add media-storage tag (large media libraries -- plex/jellyfin/9router are explicitly the final migration wave per the Obsidian inventory notes, and worker-4 only has ~55GB free of ~84GB max already). Deliberately did NOT tag tank (no HDD there per user).

Notable: worker-4 was ALREADY carrying ~78GB of scheduled replica data across 28 replicas from the untagged 'longhorn'/general-storage class before this tag was applied (bookstack, changedetection, firefox, gatus, kioto, librechat-images, microbin, notemark, nzbget x2, paperless x3, prowlarr, radarr4k, sonarr, stash x2, tautulli, tracearr, vaultwarden, whisparr, wizarr, plus PVCs 240d90b4/2fc9ef4d/d89b5c2c) -- Longhorn was scheduling there even without the formal tag, so this patch mostly formalizes existing behavior rather than opening new territory. Worth folding into home-infra-96w.2's classification pass as a real data point.

STILL OPEN: whether cp-4 should carry storage at all. Unlike originally assumed, cp-4 is NOT a blank slate -- it already hosts live production replicas (gatus, kioto-app-data, librechat-librechat-images, paperless-data, pvc-2fc9ef4d/alertmanager, qbittorrent-gluetun-config). Setting allowScheduling=false to mirror cp-1/2/3 would now trigger real replica evictions/rebuilds, not a no-op metadata change -- needs explicit approval, not a silent default.

title: Label k8s nodes with topology.kubernetes.io/zone (atlas / elitedesk-1)
description: Add topology.kubernetes.io/zone=atlas to k3s-prod-cp-1,cp-2,cp-3,worker-1,worker-2,worker-3,worker-gpu-1. Add topology.kubernetes.io/zone=elitedesk-1 to k3s-prod-cp-4,worker-4. Confirms in Longhorn as nodes.longhorn.io status.zone. This activates the already-enabled replica-zone-soft-anti-affinity setting for future scheduling decisions.
design: Pure additive kubectl label, non-disruptive: replica-auto-balance is disabled cluster-wide so no existing healthy replica will move as a side effect of adding the label. Only affects NEW replica placement (new volumes, or rebuilds of existing ones). Safe to apply without a maintenance window. Should be done via ansible role or a one-off kubectl command set -- prefer capturing it as a small ansible task/playbook so it's repo-tracked and reproducible for future nodes (se6.7 dell-sff, se6.5 proliant-1 will need the same treatment).
acceptance_criteria: kubectl get nodes.longhorn.io -n longhorn-system shows non-empty status.zone matching atlas/elitedesk-1 split for all 9 current nodes; change is repo-tracked (ansible), not a manual one-off.
notes:
2026-08-13: Applied via kubectl label (immediate, non-disruptive) to all 9 nodes -- zone=atlas on cp-1/2/3,worker-1/2/3,worker-gpu-1; zone=elitedesk-1 on cp-4,worker-4. Verified via kubectl get nodes.longhorn.io status.zone on all 9 -- correct split. Post-check: no new non-healthy/degraded volumes (3 pre-existing detached volumes unrelated -- 2 known SparkyFitness fixtures from .4, 1 unidentified detached volume pvc-4ea67c0b to fold into the .2 classification pass). replica-zone-soft-anti-affinity is now live for future scheduling/rebuild decisions.

NOT YET DONE: this is a kubectl-only label, lost if a node is redeployed/rejoins. Repo research (see below) found labels are normally applied via --node-label= in k3s_agent_args/k3s_server_args in ansible/inventories/production/host_vars/<host>.yml (pattern already used for worker-gpu-1's accelerator=nvidia label), which requires a k3s service restart per node to take effect. host_vars files for cp-4/worker-4 don't exist yet at all. Making this durable is real production risk (control-plane/etcd node restarts for cp-1/2/3) and should NOT happen casually -- split out as its own approved task, see home-infra-mi4.4.
2026-08-14 THE NODE MAPPING IN THE DESCRIPTION IS NOW WRONG -- do not apply it as written. The control plane was redistributed tonight:
  - k3s-prod-cp-2 NO LONGER EXISTS (retired and destroyed, see home-infra-se6.10)
  - k3s-prod-cp-3 MOVED from atlas to dellssf (live-migrated, see home-infra-se6.8)
  - dellssf is now a third Proxmox host in the cluster, so there is a third zone

Corrected labelling:
  topology.kubernetes.io/zone=atlas        -> cp-1, worker-1, worker-2, worker-3, worker-gpu-1
  topology.kubernetes.io/zone=elitedesk-1  -> cp-4, worker-4
  topology.kubernetes.io/zone=dellssf      -> cp-3

Note the zones are now genuinely uneven: atlas holds 5 of the 8 nodes and ALL four non-CP workers, while dellssf contributes only a control-plane node and elitedesk-1 has the single non-atlas worker. Longhorn's replica-zone-soft-anti-affinity can therefore only spread replicas between atlas and elitedesk-1 in practice, since cp nodes carry no storage. Worth factoring into this epic's expectations -- real cross-host replica redundancy still depends on adding worker capacity off atlas.

title: Longhorn cross-host replica zone spread: atlas <-> elitedesk-1
description: Pivot from home-infra-96w's single-replica shrink plan: for most existing 2-3 replica volumes, spread replicas across physical hosts (atlas vs elitedesk-1) instead of reducing to N=1, so redundancy is real against a host failure. Triggered 2026-08-13 when the user bought 2x 2.5G ethernet adapters (arriving 2026-08-14 morning) to make cross-host Longhorn replication traffic viable. Session-scoped: pause new home-infra-96w one-replica migration nominations; do NOT touch the 7 PVCs already migrated to longhorn-one-replica-flash/tank (Memos, Linkding, Affine x2, Hoarder x3) or vault-raft (stays N=1, sacred, see home-infra-96w.3).
design: Longhorn already has replica-zone-soft-anti-affinity=true (cluster-wide setting, been on 107d) but it is currently a NO-OP because no Kubernetes node carries a topology.kubernetes.io/zone label -- Longhorn Node status.zone is empty for every node. Fix requires: (1) label k8s nodes with zone=atlas for cp-1/2/3,worker-1/2/3,worker-gpu-1 and zone=elitedesk-1 for cp-4,worker-4 -- pure metadata, non-disruptive, replica-auto-balance is disabled so existing healthy replicas will NOT move just because labels appear; (2) elitedesk-1's Longhorn disks currently have ZERO tags (worker-4: default-disk-3ce0350e5cb01803, cp-4: default-disk-3ce0350e5cb01803, both untagged) so they are only eligible for the untagged 'longhorn' StorageClass today, NOT longhorn-tank/longhorn-flash/longhorn-one-replica-* which all use disk selectors -- need to decide what tier tag(s) to apply to worker-4's dedicated 200G disk before tagged-class volumes can spread there; (3) open question whether cp-4 (4c/8GB, no dedicated Longhorn disk mentioned in hardware handoff) should carry storage at all -- cp-1/2/3 all have allowScheduling=false, cp-4 currently has allowScheduling=true with no tags, worth mirroring the cp-1/2/3 pattern and keeping storage only on worker-4. Baseline network is still 1GbE tonight (2.5G adapters arrive tomorrow); user explicitly accepted temporary slowness. A bounded single-volume replica relocation test (delete one replica CR, let Longhorn reschedule -- the exact technique already proven safe today on the Prometheus volume pvc-66b783c7) would give real rebuild-duration baseline data on 1GbE before the 2.5G upgrade, without needing a cluster-wide policy flip.
notes:
2026-08-13 continued: cp-4 fully drained via Longhorn native eviction (evictionRequested=true then reset to false once empty, allowScheduling stayed false) -- confirmed by user decision "the CP node should not have any replicas... storage on that physical host lives via worker-4 only." All 6 replicas (kioto-app-data, librechat-librechat-images, librechat-meilisearch, paperless-data, alertmanager pvc-2fc9ef4d, qbittorrent-gluetun-config) relocated cleanly, 103/103 volumes healthy throughout, zero manual intervention needed beyond the single evictionRequested flag flip. cp-4 now mirrors cp-1/2/3 exactly: allowScheduling=false, evictionRequested=false, no tags.

Tank clarification from user: longhorn-tank is backed by ONE shared HDD-only ZFS pool on atlas across worker-1/2/3's tank disks, and that pool has its own redundancy (mirror/RAIDZ) independent of Longhorn replica placement. So co-located tank replicas (both on atlas) already have real disk-failure protection -- the "same host = fake redundancy" framing does NOT apply to longhorn-tank/longhorn-steady/longhorn-vault-raft (all diskSelector=tank). Only applies to flash/general/untagged tiers where atlas disks are independent per-VM, not a shared redundant pool.

Network topology research (read-only, both repo grep and live ethtool checks):
- No VLAN anywhere in atlas's Terraform network config; all atlas VMs sit untagged on vmbr0. Same-physical-host VM-to-VM traffic (e.g. worker-1<->worker-2) never leaves the box -- switched entirely in-kernel by the Linux bridge. Flannel VXLAN encapsulation between same-host nodes also resolves locally via the shared L2 bridge. So same-host Longhorn replication has ZERO physical-network cost today; any overhead is CPU/software (VXLAN encap, iptables/conntrack), not wire distance -- this ruled out the user's "shared storage pool to avoid virtual network traffic" idea as solving a real bottleneck (also Longhorn doesn't support multiple nodes safely sharing one backing replica anyway).
- Confirmed live via ansible ad-hoc + ethtool: atlas's active physical NIC (nic0, carries vmbr0/all VM traffic) is ALREADY negotiating 2500Mb/s on the 2.5G switch today. nic1/nic2 (atlas's 2 built-in 1G ports) are unplugged/unused.
- Confirmed live on elitedesk-1 (172.20.20.7, ad-hoc since it's not yet in ansible/inventories/proxmox/hosts.yml): built-in nic0 currently at 1000Mb/s (the bottleneck), PLUS a USB NIC interface enx0c37965cbfe2 already recognized by the kernel but down/no-link -- almost certainly one of the purchased 2.5G adapters already seated in the USB port, just not yet cabled to a switch.
- User's home network: 2x 8-port switches, one 1G (currently idle/unused), one 2.5G (everything currently plugged into it). Plan is atlas (native 2.5G, already connected) + elitedesk-1 and dell-sff (each getting a USB 2.5G adapter, built-in NICs are 1G) all landing on the 2.5G switch. dell-sff is compute-only/no-Longhorn per home-infra-se6.7, so its 2.5G upgrade matters for other things (e.g. qm migrate for haos/pbs, se6.9) not this epic; only elitedesk-1's link matters for Longhorn cross-host replication.
- Conclusion: once elitedesk-1's USB adapter is cabled to the 2.5G switch tomorrow, atlas<->elitedesk-1 should go from a 1G-capped path today to a full 2.5G path end-to-end (atlas side already ready, no further atlas-side work needed).

Net effect of tonight's changes so far: zone labels active on all 9 nodes; worker-4 tagged flash+general-storage; cp-4 fully evicted of storage duty. home-infra-mi4.3 (bounded relocation test) still needs a volume pick + approval before executing -- still on today's 1GbE elitedesk-1 link since the USB adapter isn't cabled yet.

2. Align Proxmox versions first (upgrade atlas to 9.2.10, or hold elitedesk-1 back) -- mismatched versions across corosync members isn't recommended.

notes: 2026-08-13/14 gotcha found and fixed: crowdsec-agent DaemonSet crash-loops on any newly-joined node ("API error: ent: machine not found", 401) because each agent authenticates to crowdsec-lapi as a "machine" named after the k8s node name (spec.nodeName) with a shared static password, and the LAPI requires each machine to be explicitly registered first via `cscli machines add`. New nodes are never auto-registered. title: promote-everlyera.sh: other-environment guard is an unanchored repo-wide grep
description:
scripts/maintenance/promote-everlyera.sh line 102:

  git -C $REPO diff --name-only | grep -q overlays/$OTHER_ENV && die 'refusing: the $OTHER_ENV overlay also changed'

The grep is not scoped to the everlyera app, so ANY application's overlays/prod or overlays/stage path in the working tree trips it.

Hit on 2026-08-06 promoting everlyera 0.11.1 to stage: refused with 'the prod overlay also changed' while the everlyera prod overlay was clean at 0.10.1. The actual match was an unrelated in-flight change to argocd/manifests/monitoring-config/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml.

The guard is worth keeping — it exists so a promote cannot ride along with an unreviewed change to the other environment — but it should only consider the everlyera app:

  grep -q argocd/manifests/everlyera/overlays/$OTHER_ENV

The failure mode is safe (it refuses rather than proceeds) but it blocks any everlyera release whenever unrelated cluster work is uncommitted, which is often.

Second, smaller defect: the abort happens AFTER the overlay file has been rewritten, so a refused run leaves the stage overlay edit sitting in the working tree and the caller has to revert it by hand. Either write the file after the guards, or trap and restore on failure.

notes: 2026-08-13: Epic paused pending home-infra-mi4 (cross-host zone-spread design). Rationale: classification work this session found virtually every N>=2 PVC in the fleet has ALL replicas on atlas nodes (cp-1/2/3, worker-1/2/3, worker-gpu-1) -- current redundancy is mostly fake against a host failure regardless of replica count. User's new 2.5G links make real cross-host spread (not just shrinking to N=1) viable. .1 and the 5-app pilot wave remain valid and closed/done; .2/.3/.4 read-only classification work can continue in parallel since it's non-destructive either way, but no new migration waves execute until home-infra-mi4 lands a recommendation.
close_reason:
SUPERSEDED 2026-08-14 by home-infra-mi4 (cross-host replica zone spread). Confirmed with Pierce.

The premise no longer holds. This epic existed to shrink Longhorn PVCs to one replica because, with every node on a single physical host, an N=2 volume's second copy bought nothing against host failure -- it was fake redundancy consuming flash. Once elitedesk-1 and then dellssf joined the Proxmox cluster, N=2 spread across hosts became real redundancy, so shrinking stopped making sense. The epic was already paused on 2026-08-13 pending mi4's recommendation; mi4 landed, and the answer was spread rather than shrink.

The live cluster already reflects the reversal, verified 2026-08-14:
  - Only 4 volumes are N=1, and all are vault-raft (N=1 by design; Raft replicates itself)
  - All 7 PVCs this epic migrated are back at N=2

title: Pin MiniMax-M2.7 as always-loaded (preload + no TTL)
description:
User wants MiniMax-M2.7-UD-Q4_K_M to be the only model that ever runs on the GPU worker for the foreseeable future and to never pay the ~15-min mlock cold-load cost again after a pod restart. Achieved with two llama-swap features (verified against upstream config.example.yaml):

- globalTTL: 0 at top level (default never-unload)
- hooks.on_startup.preload: [MiniMax-M2.7-UD-Q4_K_M] (load at startup, not on first request)
- removed the per-model ttl: 3600 from MiniMax (inherits 0)

Other models still have their explicit ttl values so they retain swap-out behaviour for the rare case the operator manually loads one. Pinning MiniMax means manually-requested alternatives will be blocked while it holds GPU layers + 138 GiB locked RAM — acceptable per user direction.
close_reason: Pushed in commits eba66de + 3ab50b1. globalTTL: 0 + hooks.on_startup.preload pins MiniMax-M2.7-UD-Q4_K_M permanently in memory and reloads it during pod rollout instead of on first user request. The new metrics-sidecar in the llama-cpp pod polls llama-swap /running, scrapes /upstream/<active model>/metrics, and aggregates with the host llamaswap_* gauges into a single /metrics endpoint on port 9090. ServiceMonitor in monitoring-config scrapes it as job=llama-cpp instance=cluster (relabel). Dashboard ConfigMap (grafana_dashboard=1) ships 13 panels with instance + model template dropdowns. Verified end-to-end: 11 llamacpp:* metrics + llamacpp_active_model_info flow through the sidecar, Prometheus target is UP, MiniMax preloaded in ~8s due to warm page cache. PC instance to be added later via additionalScrapeConfigs against llama-swap's peers feature or direct scrape.

title: Switch MiniMax-M2.7 to --mlock to eliminate HDD random-fault penalty
description: Observed 2026-06-03: MiniMax-M2.7-UD-Q4_K_M ran for 29 minutes after first chat request and only paged in 25.7 GiB of 148.9 GiB mmap (17%), driving 5071 major page faults/sec on the GPU worker (NodeMemoryMajorPagesFaults alert). HDD random IO via lazy mmap is the bottleneck. Plan: add --mlock so the kernel forces all weights into RAM once at load time (sequential reads), add IPC_LOCK capability so the container can lift its 8 MiB RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, bump container memory request 80->150 and limit 150->170 GiB, bump healthCheckTimeout 1800->2700s for first cold load. Pod will roll via ArgoCD when configmap hash changes.
close_reason: Pod rolled to b395f3c. Container has IPC_LOCK (CapEff bit 14 set, verified 0xa80465fb includes 0x4000), memory limits raised to 150Gi/170Gi, MiniMax config has --mlock, healthCheckTimeout 2700s. Next /v1/chat/completions to MiniMax-M2.7-UD-Q4_K_M will trigger a fresh load that pulls the full 138 GiB into RAM sequentially via mlock instead of random-fault dribbling.

Need to cordon/drain k3s-prod-worker-gpu-1, qm shutdown 107 on atlas, then qm start. Verify free -m inside the guest reports ~200 GiB, then uncordon. Watch atlas host memory afterwards: total commit will hit ~307 GiB of 322 GiB available.

4. Address the remaining tracked app manifest directory under argocd/manifests/ that relied on the cluster default for PVCs, plus argocd/manifests/llama-cpp/* (storageClassName: '' for static PV). Add explicit SC + a one-line comment explaining the choice.

5. As Phase 4 waves resolve drift, drop the corresponding ignoreDifferences entries from the relevant ArgoCD Application manifests:
   - argocd/apps/prod/paperless.yaml (paperless-db PVC SC ignore)
   - argocd/apps/prod/sparkyfitness.yaml (PVC labels + SC ignore)
   - vault.yaml's StatefulSet labels ignore
acceptance_criteria: grep -r 'ignoreDifferences' argocd/apps/prod/ shows only entries with inline comments referencing still-open bd issues + Kubernetes immutability constraints. No 'we patched live, ignore' entries. README accurate. Quick fixes committed and ArgoCD Synced.

This satisfies the comment-hygiene part of kd3; app sync state still needs verification once the branch changes are applied.

title: Phase 2: scripts/maintenance/audit-storage-policy.sh
description:
Build the policy-gate audit script. Models on scripts/maintenance/verify-cross-pool-placement.sh for style.

For every Longhorn PVC, compares against policy and reports:
  - expected SC vs actual SC (from kubectl get pvc)
  - expected replica count vs actual (from Longhorn Volume CR spec.numberOfReplicas)
  - expected backup groups vs actual (from PVC metadata labels)
  - any runtime patches present (Volume CR spec.diskSelector, replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity, numberOfReplicas overrides — should be empty for everything except SC-defined cases)

Output: markdown table with ✅/❌ per column, summary count at the end.
Exit 0 if everything matches, 1 otherwise.

Policy lives in the script as a Bash associative array keyed on namespace/pvc. Explicit list, no inference. Adding a new app = update this script and the policy doc together (link them in comments).

The audit script IS the cleanup gate — until it exits 0 on two consecutive runs 24h apart, the cleanup isn't done.
acceptance_criteria: Script exists, executable, follows verify-cross-pool-placement.sh style. Runs against current cluster and produces a markdown report with at least 80% of PVCs covered by an entry in the policy array. Used in subsequent waves' acceptance criteria.
notes: Investigated orphan volume surfaced by the audit: pvc-ee3bfcbe-5a8e-4238-bdb7-4d67ba93a6d1 belongs to namespace vault / pvc data-vault-0, created 2026-04-28, still healthy in Longhorn, but there is no current vault namespace, no PV, and no repo reference. It appears to be a leftover from the old non-raft Vault deployment and should be handled as separate cleanup work rather than folded into the public policy inventory.
close_reason: audit-storage-policy.sh and the committed public inventory landed on storage-policy-cleanup-plan; the script is executable, reports SC/replica/backup/runtime-patch drift, supports a local private override file, and currently reaches full live PVC coverage with one separately tracked orphan volume blocker.

title: Phase 1: write docs/operations/storage-policy.md with decision table
description:
Create the storage policy doc. Decision table from the plan (review/adjust during execution):

| App class | SC | replicas | Backup groups |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vault raft member | longhorn-vault-raft | 1 | hourly+daily+weekly |
| Heavy continuous writer (DBs/TSDBs/log stores) | longhorn-tank | 2 | hourly+daily+weekly (Loki: skip hourly) |
| Read-fast, write-rarely | longhorn-flash | 2 | daily+weekly |
| Single-pod no-HA needs durability | longhorn-redundant | 3 | daily+weekly |
| Catch-all | longhorn (default) | 3 | daily+weekly |
| Media on GPU worker | longhorn-media | 3 | daily+weekly |
| Static PV | static | n/a | n/a |

Principles to include verbatim:
1. 'Heavy writer' = sustained >X IOPS / >Y bytes/s 95th — define X/Y after a Prometheus dig with the new Atlas per-drive panels (commit 7abc14b).
2. Replica count is per-SC; volumes inherit at creation; changing requires PVC recreation.
3. longhorn-flash / longhorn-tank are pinned by SC, not by per-volume diskSelector. Every runtime diskSelector patch = wrong SC.
4. Labels are policy: every PVC needs explicit backup-group labels in manifest, unless explicitly opted out with annotation + bd-issue reference (memos, Loki).
5. Default SC is for apps with no special needs; putting a write-heavy DB there is a bug.

Also need short sections on:
  - Flash pool IOPS budget (link Grafana panel)
  - longhorn-vault-raft pattern vs longhorn-redundant
  - Restored-from-backup quirks (memos-workaround-2026-05-29)
acceptance_criteria: docs/operations/storage-policy.md exists; cluster-operations.md Longhorn section trimmed and links to it; policy table is concrete (no TBDs); user has reviewed and signed off in the cleanup session
notes: User approved intent-based canonical StorageClass names for the target policy: longhorn-general (legacy longhorn), longhorn-fast (legacy longhorn-flash), longhorn-steady (legacy longhorn-tank), longhorn-singleton (legacy longhorn-redundant); memos stays in the fast class. Branch work now documents the naming transition explicitly.
close_reason: User reviewed and approved the storage policy, canonical StorageClass names, and memos staying in the fast class; docs landed in repo and branch work documents the naming transition.

title: Flash IOPS budget: identify+migrate other heavy-write apps to tank
description:
Today's incident (2026-05-31) showed the Atlas flash zpool is over-committed on sustained IOPS. The 6 PVCs we already moved (3 vault, paperless-db, prometheus, loki) gave breathing room but more candidates likely exist.

Apps to evaluate for tank pinning:
  - immich-db (Postgres, heavy writes)
  - librechat-mongodb (Mongo, writes)
  - radarr/sonarr/prowlarr plus one private *arr config (SQLite log writes, surprisingly high IOPS)
  - bookstack-db-data (MariaDB writes)
  - alertmanager-* (current SC: longhorn, on 2 flash + 1 tank from yov)

For each: check write rate via Longhorn UI or node-exporter, decide whether tank-pinning fits 'heavy-write, throughput-bound' principle. Apps that need flash latency for reads (memos, seerr-config, vaultwarden) can stay on flash.

This is the 'don't put heavy writers on flash' lesson from 2026-05-31 generalized. Related: home-infra-dil (SLOG would help mitigate but doesn't replace right-pool placement).

Acceptance: list of all PVCs with their write-volume classification + recommended SC; PRs for the changes.
close_reason: Superseded by home-infra-wdy umbrella. The new storage-policy.md + audit-storage-policy.sh under that umbrella encode the lesson (write-heavy → tank, with measurable threshold via the Atlas per-drive Grafana panels) more concretely than this open-ended review issue.

title: Move Longhorn StorageClasses to argocd/manifests/ (out of Ansible)
description:
Today the longhorn / longhorn-flash / longhorn-tank StorageClasses are built as Jinja-templated YAML strings and applied via inline 'kubectl apply -f - <<EOF ... EOF' shell tasks in ansible/roles/cluster_platform/tasks/longhorn-storage-config.yml:99-259.

Meanwhile, a peer StorageClass (longhorn-redundant) already lives declaratively at argocd/manifests/longhorn-redundant-sc/base/storageclass.yaml.

This is split-brain ownership: Ansible can clobber an ArgoCD-managed SC and vice versa. Operators editing one source-of-truth may have their change silently reverted by the other.

Parent: home-infra-nwr.
design:
Create argocd/manifests/longhorn-storage-classes/base/ with one YAML per SC:
- longhorn.yaml (default, no diskSelector)
- longhorn-flash.yaml (diskSelector: flash)
- longhorn-tank.yaml (diskSelector: tank)

Use kustomize overlay pattern if numberOfReplicas needs to vary by env (base + overlays/prod, overlays/test). Match the existing argocd/manifests/longhorn-redundant-sc/ structure for consistency.

Add an ArgoCD Application under argocd/apps/<env>/ to reconcile the new manifests directory. Decide whether to put it in prod-only, test-only, or both per-env.

Remove the corresponding build/apply tasks from ansible/roles/cluster_platform/tasks/longhorn-storage-config.yml:99-259. Helm values for the chart (Longhorn settings, backup target URL, replica count default at the Longhorn-system level) stay in Ansible — only the StorageClass objects move.
acceptance_criteria:
- ArgoCD app for SCs is Healthy/Synced on prod and test
- Ansible run no longer touches StorageClass objects (verifiable via dry-run)
- Manually deleting a SC causes ArgoCD to recreate it within reconciliation interval
- SC parameters byte-for-byte match pre-migration state (verified via kubectl get sc <name> -o yaml diff)
- If home-infra-rd0 (Epic 1 .b) lands first, accommodate the N=3 + diskSoftAntiAffinity change in the new manifest
notes: Migration completed 2026-05-30. ArgoCD app longhorn-storage-classes is Synced+Healthy on prod. Discovery: ArgoCD's Replace=true syncOption uses kubectl replace (without --force), which still fails on immutable SC.parameters. Had to manually delete the longhorn SC + the longhorn-storageclass configmap before ArgoCD could create the SC with new params. Once the longhorn-storageclass configmap was gone, longhorn-manager stopped recreating the SC and ArgoCD took clean ownership. The helm value persistence.defaultClass: false is in main but not yet applied to the live release; the configmap deletion gives the equivalent end state until the next Ansible run.
close_reason: ArgoCD adopted all 3 SCs; longhorn-storageclass configmap removed; SC ownership transferred.

title: Collapse longhorn-tank-disk.yml and longhorn-data-disk.yml into one parameterized task
description:
ansible/roles/k3s/tasks/longhorn-tank-disk.yml (49 lines) and longhorn-data-disk.yml (49 lines) are 90%+ duplicates. The pattern is: stat → fail-if-missing → mkfs.ext4 → blkid → mkdir → mount with nofail. Only variable names and one hard-coded mount path (/var/lib/longhorn in the data-disk task) differ.

Parent: home-infra-nwr. Blocked by epic2-A so the slot-var work is in place before refactoring.
design:
Create ansible/roles/k3s/tasks/longhorn-disk.yml parameterized on:
- disk_device (input, required)
- disk_path (input, required)
- disk_label (input, required — used for register: var name suffix and human-readable messages)

In main.yml, replace the two existing include_tasks with two parameterized invocations:
  - include_tasks: longhorn-disk.yml
    vars:
      disk_device: '{{ longhorn_data_disk_device }}'
      disk_path: /var/lib/longhorn
      disk_label: data
  - include_tasks: longhorn-disk.yml
    vars:
      disk_device: '{{ longhorn_tank_disk_device }}'
      disk_path: '{{ longhorn_tank_disk_path }}'
      disk_label: tank

Delete longhorn-tank-disk.yml and longhorn-data-disk.yml after the new task is verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two task files deleted, one new task file added (net -1 file)
- Both mounts (/var/lib/longhorn on hosts that use it, /mnt/longhorn-tank on workers) still produced correctly
- Idempotent re-run of the role shows zero changes
- Comments preserved (nofail rationale, etc.)
close_reason: Unified longhorn-disk.yml replaces both old task files. Passes ansible-playbook --syntax-check. Full live-run verification deferred to next ansible execution.

title: DRY Longhorn device paths into group_vars + parameterize SCSI slot
description:
Today longhorn_tank_disk_device: /dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi2 repeats verbatim across ansible/inventories/production/host_vars/k3s-prod-worker-{1,2,3}.yml:11 (verified by diff — only the worker-number comment differs).

Three problems:
1. DRY violation: changing the SCSI slot requires editing three files
2. Hard-coded QEMU SCSI ID is fragile across cluster rebuilds
3. Already-parameterized in Terraform (terraform/modules/proxmox-cloudinit-nodes/variables.tf exposes data_disk_slot), but Ansible has no matching var

Parent: home-infra-nwr.
design:
Add to ansible/group_vars/k3s_cluster.yml:
- longhorn_tank_disk_slot: 'scsi2'
- longhorn_data_disk_slot: 'scsi1'  (preserves current behavior for hosts that mount /var/lib/longhorn on a dedicated disk)
- longhorn_disk_device_template: '/dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-{slot}'

In ansible/roles/k3s/tasks/main.yml (or the unified disk task from epic2-B), derive longhorn_tank_disk_device and longhorn_data_disk_device via a Jinja replace or set_fact:
  vars:
    longhorn_tank_disk_device: '{{ longhorn_disk_device_template | replace("{slot}", longhorn_tank_disk_slot) }}'

Delete the per-host overrides for the standard 3 workers. Keep override capability for k3s-prod-worker-gpu-1 which has tank only and a different layout — it can set longhorn_tank_disk_slot in its host_vars.
acceptance_criteria:
- All three k3s-prod-worker-{1,2,3}.yml host_vars no longer mention longhorn_tank_disk_device
- Ansible run on prod still produces a working mount on /mnt/longhorn-tank
- GPU worker (worker-gpu-1) still gets its custom slot via host_vars override
- Variable name aligns with terraform var data_disk_slot for consistency
close_reason: Slot var landed in group_vars/k3s_cluster_prod_workers.yml; role derives device path from template+slot. Verified resolution across all 7 hosts: CP nodes get undef (task skipped), worker-1/2/3 get scsi2 (task runs), worker-gpu-1 opts out via host_vars (task skipped).

title: Migrate existing flash-only / same-pool volumes to cross-pool placement
description:
Run scripts/maintenance/migrate-volumes-to-cross-pool.sh against the ~46 volumes currently flagged by home-infra-n4r (flash-only or same-pool placement).

CRITICAL: respect the batch-restore cascade lesson (memory longhorn-batch-restore-cascade-2026-05-30):
- One volume at a time
- Wait for healthy attach + actualSize > 0 before continuing
- Verify the workload's pod comes up healthy
- Watch IM memory and event rate between iterations
- DO NOT chain N invasive ops in a tight loop

If ArgoCD auto-sync is paused on apps during migration, re-pause it before the next iteration (the migrate script may re-enable auto-sync on the target app).

Blocked by 22f.b so the new SC parameters drive the 2→3 bounce.
acceptance_criteria:
- All volumes flagged by verify-cross-pool-placement.sh on the prod cluster cleared
- home-infra-n4r closes
- No new SIGBUS / IM disruption incidents during the migration window
- Log of which volumes were migrated and when, attached to the issue notes
notes:
Session complete 2026-05-30. Migrated 25 of 27 misplaced volumes to N=3 cross-pool.

Final state:
- 25 migrated: all ended 2-tank + 1-flash (preferred) or 2-flash + 1-tank (originally-all-flash subset, user-accepted reverse)
- 1 explicit skip: memos-data-v3 (SIGBUS on workers 1/3 per bd memory memos-workaround-2026-05-29)
- 1 audit-flagged remaining: memos-data-v3 only

All 3 vault pods stayed unsealed throughout, leader unchanged. All 7 IMs Running. No stopped zombie replicas after cleanup.

Methodology lessons captured here for future operators:

1. The migrate-volumes-to-cross-pool.sh script's set_pool_scheduling disables ENTIRE pool cluster-wide. Other volumes rebuilding during the window can fail and rebuild on the wrong pool, causing regressions (jellyfin-config-rdn regressed twice during this session for this reason).

2. Mitigation that worked: minimize the disabled window. The fast pattern is: disable pool → patch volume to N=3 → wait for the new replica to be SCHEDULED (not synced) → re-enable pool. This shrinks the window to seconds even for large volumes.

3. For volumes already at N=3 same-pool (like firefox-gluetun-config, hoarder-meilisearch, librechat-images, jellyfin-config-rdn): use delete-tank-replica + scheduling-force approach instead of bump. Same fast-window pattern works.

4. Large volumes (>50GB) are especially prone to rebuild timeouts if interrupted. Do them last and in isolation. jellyfin-config-rdn took ~10 min to fully sync at 60GB after the procedure.

5. Vault migrations: verify all 3 raft pods unsealed before each PVC; do standby pods first, leader last. No leader transitions observed during this session.

6. Soft anti-affinity is a tiebreaker, not a guarantee. Cluster-level replica-disk-soft-anti-affinity=true didn't prevent same-pool placement on N=3 bumps. --force-flash / --force-tank is the reliable mechanism.
close_reason: 25 of 27 misplaced volumes migrated to cross-pool N=3. memos-data-v3 explicitly skipped (SIGBUS). Methodology lessons captured in notes.

title: Update default longhorn SC to numberOfReplicas=3 + replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity
description:
Mutate the default longhorn StorageClass: numberOfReplicas=3, add replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=true. Leave longhorn-flash and longhorn-tank at numberOfReplicas=2 — they are already pinned by design and don't need the cross-pool spread.

File touched depends on whether home-infra-nwr (Epic 2) Sub-issue C (move SCs to ArgoCD) lands first:
- If yes: edit argocd/manifests/longhorn-storage-classes/base/longhorn.yaml
- If not yet: edit ansible/roles/cluster_platform/tasks/longhorn-storage-config.yml:99-127

Blocked by the spike (22f.a) for the go decision, and ideally by epic2-C so we don't have to rewrite the change later.
acceptance_criteria:
- New PVCs created against the default SC come up with 3 replicas
- verify-cross-pool-placement.sh exits 0 for newly provisioned volumes
- No regressions on longhorn-flash / longhorn-tank pinned volumes
- Prod ArgoCD app (or Ansible run) is healthy/synced
notes: Verified live 2026-05-30: created throwaway PVC in rd0-verify ns; replicas landed deterministic 2-tank + 1-flash (worker-3 flash, workers 1+2 tank). Matches spike result from home-infra-pwo. New PVCs on the default longhorn SC now get this layout automatically. Existing 27 same-pool volumes still need home-infra-yov migration.
close_reason: Default longhorn SC mutated to N=3 + replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=enabled via ArgoCD; new-PVC placement verified.

title: Spike: validate replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity behavior on test cluster
description:
Before mutating the prod default StorageClass, validate that numberOfReplicas=3 + replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=true actually soft-spreads replicas across flash/tank-tagged disks on the test cluster.

Steps:
1. Tag test-cluster disks 'flash' and 'tank' the same way prod does (or pick two existing tags).
2. Create a test SC with numberOfReplicas=3, replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=true.
3. Provision 3–5 throwaway PVCs using that SC.
4. Run scripts/maintenance/verify-cross-pool-placement.sh against the test cluster and confirm it flags none of the new volumes.
5. Capture observed replica distribution (which pool each replica landed on) for each volume.
6. Bounce one replica (delete a replica CR) and observe whether rebuild respects anti-affinity.

Watch for:
- IM disruption / SIGBUS during replica bounce (memory longhorn-batch-restore-cascade-2026-05-30)
- Cases where all 3 replicas still land on the same pool despite the affinity hint
acceptance_criteria:
- handoff/ or docs/operations/ updated with observed placement distribution and any caveats
- Explicit go/no-go decision recorded for proceeding to home-infra-22f.b
- If no-go, alternative approach captured in this issue's notes before closing
notes:
Spike complete 2026-05-30. Findings:

1. SC parameter accepts enabled/disabled/ignored, NOT true/false. Using 'true' produced 'invalid ReplicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity setting: true' from csi-provisioner. Final value: replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity: "enabled".

2. All 3 throwaway PVCs landed 2-tank + 1-flash. Identical placement (flash on worker-3, tank on workers 1+2) across all three — scheduler is deterministic on uniform topology.

3. verify-cross-pool-placement.sh correctly classified spike volumes as not-misplaced. Confirmed 27 same-pool volumes existing out of 71 checked (38% misplacement rate without anti-affinity).

4. Replica rebuild behavior on disk failure NOT tested in this spike — observe during home-infra-rd0 rollout.

5. Tiny audit-script polish: KUBECTL="kubectl --context=foo" indirection breaks command -v. Not blocking.

Decision: GO for home-infra-rd0 with replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=enabled.

Full writeup: handoff/2026-05-30-cross-pool-replica-anti-affinity-spike.md
close_reason: Spike validated. Decision GO for home-infra-rd0 with replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=enabled. Findings in handoff/2026-05-30-cross-pool-replica-anti-affinity-spike.md and issue notes.

title: Longhorn cross-pool Ansible hygiene cleanup
description:
Umbrella for hygiene issues introduced or surfaced by commit de9eef4 (cross-pool storage architecture) and related Longhorn commits (9206e3f, e110034, 6c7ab98, 02f28cd).

Sub-issues cover:
- Hard-coded SCSI by-id device paths in three identical worker host_vars
- Duplicated Ansible disk tasks (longhorn-tank-disk.yml ~90% copy of longhorn-data-disk.yml)
- Split-brain StorageClass ownership: Ansible heredoc kubectl apply vs ArgoCD declarative manifests for peer SCs
- Shell-based Longhorn settings management (kubectl patch loops with failed_when=false, no idempotency)
- Unmanaged flash-disk mount (currently in fstab outside Ansible)

The parent issue exists to group these so they can be claimed and closed individually but reviewed as one cleanup wave.
design:
Suggested execution order:
1. epic2-A (DRY device paths to group_vars + slot var)
2. epic2-C (move SCs to argocd/manifests/) — coordinates with home-infra-22f.b
3. epic2-B (collapse longhorn-disk.yml unified task) — uses A's cleaner var model
4. epic2-E (bring flash disk under Ansible) — uses unified task from B
5. epic2-D (Helm values instead of kubectl patch)
6. epic2-F (Ansible wrapper for migrate-volumes script) — deferred P4

Sub-issues link via bd dep add so bd ready surfaces only those without blockers.
acceptance_criteria:
- All five sub-issues (A–E) closed
- epic2-F filed and deferred (or closed as 'won't do' if migration cycle proves unnecessary)
- A fresh-clone Ansible run on a rebuilt worker produces working /mnt/longhorn-flash and /mnt/longhorn-tank with no per-host device-path overrides for the standard 3 workers
- No kubectl patch setting calls remain in cluster_platform role
- Default longhorn SC + longhorn-flash + longhorn-tank all managed by ArgoCD

title: Cross-pool replica placement: bump default SC to numberOfReplicas=3 with disk anti-affinity
description:
The cross-pool architecture from commit de9eef4 ships with the default `longhorn` StorageClass at numberOfReplicas=2 and no diskSelector (ansible/roles/cluster_platform/tasks/longhorn-storage-config.yml:113). With two replicas and best-effort scheduling across 6 disks (3 flash + 3 tank), both replicas can still land on the same pool — defeating the resilience goal that motivated the cross-pool design.

Tank headroom is ~935G; current flash-scheduled is ~624G. Bumping the default to numberOfReplicas=3 with replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=true should soft-spread replicas across disk types, approximating a 2-tank + 1-flash intent without needing a mutating webhook. scripts/maintenance/verify-cross-pool-placement.sh already audits same-pool placement and stays the drift gate.

Parent epic for replica-placement work. Sub-issues cover spike, SC mutation, existing-volume migration, and docs.
design:
Longhorn StorageClass API does not expose a per-disk-type replica count. Options considered:

- CHOSEN: numberOfReplicas=3 + replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=true — declarative, no new components, ~50% storage cost increase per volume. Soft-affinity tolerates the no-room case (a node losing its flash disk doesn't block scheduling).
- REJECTED: mutating admission webhook to rewrite per-volume placement — operational burden, new failure mode.
- REJECTED: per-volume annotations / manual pinning — doesn't scale to 46+ existing volumes (see home-infra-n4r).

Existing volumes migrate via scripts/maintenance/migrate-volumes-to-cross-pool.sh (2→3 bounce). Batch-restore caution per memory longhorn-batch-restore-cascade-2026-05-30 applies: one volume at a time, observe IM memory + event rate, then continue.
acceptance_criteria:
- All four sub-issues filed and linked as blocking-deps
- Spike sub-issue lands a documented test-cluster run showing replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity behavior matches expectations
- After the SC-mutation and migration sub-issues land, verify-cross-pool-placement.sh exits 0 on prod
- home-infra-n4r (46 flash-only volumes) closes as a consequence
close_reason: All sub-issues closed: spike (pwo), SC mutation (rd0), volume migration (yov, 25 of 27 + 1 explicit skip), docs (60r). Cross-pool replica placement is the cluster's steady state. verify-cross-pool-placement.sh exits 0 modulo memos-data-v3 (permanent skip).

notes: Done: scripts/maintenance/verify-cross-pool-placement.sh — walks volumes, joins disk-id with disk-tag via spec.disks (status.diskStatus has no tags), categorizes pools, flags volumes whose replicas all land on same pool when SC is 'longhorn'. Initial run showed 44 misplaced; after bumping r=1 volumes back to r=2, 20 became cross-pool organically. Committed in de9eef4.

title: Combine Proxmox Hosts and Proxmox via Prometheus dashboards into one
description:
We currently have two separate Proxmox dashboards in Grafana:
1. 'Proxmox Hosts' (custom, home-infra built) — shows node-exporter metrics: LVM thin-pool data/metadata, VG free space, CPU, memory, load, disk IO, network IO, filesystem usage. Uses job=proxmox-node-exporter and proxmox_host labels.
2. 'Proxmox via Prometheus' (community dashboard 10347) — shows pve-exporter metrics: VM/CT resource allocation summary, guest CPU/memory/disk/network, storage usage/space allocation. Uses job=proxmox-pve-exporter and instance label (now set to hostname).

Goal: merge the key panels from both into a single 'Proxmox Hosts' dashboard so there's one pane of glass for Proxmox infrastructure health. Keep the LVM thin-pool risk panels front and center since that's our primary protection target. Remove the old 'Proxmox via Prometheus' dashboard ConfigMap when done.
close_reason: Closed

title: Generate Proxmox monitoring targets from Ansible inventory
description: The Proxmox host monitoring resources were generalized to proxmox-node-exporter and relabel endpoint hostnames into proxmox_host, but raw Kubernetes Endpoints are excluded by ArgoCD settings, so the live endpoint currently requires manual kubectl apply. Add a reusable inventory-driven mechanism so future Proxmox hosts can be added in ansible/inventories/proxmox/hosts.yml and monitoring targets are generated/applied consistently.

title: Surgically recover 4 stuck Longhorn volumes after migration churn
description:
After the aggressive parallel tank→flash Longhorn migration (home-infra-sbd) on 2026-05-23, several volumes ended up stuck in attach/detach cycles when the Longhorn instance managers crashed under sustained rebuild load. We cleaned up 32 BAD replicas (stopped+failed) and recovered 4 volumes (changedetection-data, radarr-config, radarr4k-config, plus partial vault-raft-0/1), but 4 remain:

1. data-vault-raft-2 — cycling detaching/faulted ↔ attaching/unknown. 1 healthy replica on worker-2/flash. vault-raft-2 pod can't ContainerCreate, Vault cluster at 2/3 quorum.
2. tautulli-config — cycling. 1 healthy replica on worker-1/flash. tautulli pod ContainerCreating.
3. one private *arr config PVC — cycling. 1 healthy replica on worker-1/flash. The corresponding pod is stuck during init.
4. immich-db — both replicas failed (state=stopped, started=False). Needs backup restore.

Bonus weird-state: seerr-config has 1 replica in running-but-started-false state — Longhorn refused to delete it ('no other healthy replica available...may still contain data for recovery'). Currently detached/faulted.
design:
Recovery pattern that works most of the time (proven on 3 volumes already):
1. Delete BAD replicas: `kubectl delete replica.longhorn.io <name> -n longhorn-system`
2. Force-detach the volume: `kubectl patch volume.longhorn.io <vol> -n longhorn-system --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"nodeID":""}}'`
3. Delete stale VolumeAttachment objects referencing the PV (see HANDOFF.md for the Python one-liner)
4. Delete the engine: `kubectl delete engine.longhorn.io <vol>-e-0 -n longhorn-system`
5. Delete the requesting pod so a fresh attach is requested
6. Repeat steps 2-5 if it cycles again

For immich-db (no healthy replica): need backup restore from Longhorn's NFS-stored snapshots. Check `kubectl get backups -n longhorn-system | grep immich-db` for available restore points.

For seerr-config: the replica in running/started=False state may unstick if we wait — or could try Longhorn UI's Salvage action. If that fails, restore from backup.
acceptance_criteria:
- All 4 stuck volumes attached/healthy or attached/degraded (rebuilding)
- All affected app pods (vault-raft-2, tautulli, the private *arr app, immich-postgres, seerr) Running 1/1
- ESes not Ready count drops back to 0
- HANDOFF.md updated to reflect cleared state, or removed entirely
close_reason: All 4 originally-stuck volumes (data-vault-raft-2, tautulli-config, immich-db, seerr-config) recovered during 2026-05-23 session. Underlying causes were the longhorn-storageclass ConfigMap bug (fixed in commit e86a779), worker-2 iSCSI corruption (fixed by reboot), and the cascading rebuild-induced timeouts (fixed by sync=disabled + replicas=1 on big volumes).

title: Prometheus alert: Vault has no active leader for >5m
description:
The 2026-05-21 incident where the Vault Raft cluster sat in a no-leader state for >40 minutes was discovered only when ESO-dependent apps started failing to refresh secrets, not by an alert.

Vault exports a Prometheus metric `vault_core_active{}` (1 = active, 0 = standby/sealed). We should fire a critical alert when no pod has `vault_core_active == 1` for sustained time.

Bonus alerts to consider in the same rule group:
- vault_core_unsealed == 0 for >5m on any pod (leader-independent)
- vault_raft_replication_appendEntries_logs == 0 for >5m on standby pods (replication stalled)
design:
Vault is already scraped (it has a /sys/metrics?format=prometheus endpoint). Add a PrometheusRule under argocd/manifests/monitoring-config/.

Example rule:

  - alert: VaultClusterNoActiveLeader
    expr: max by () (vault_core_active) == 0
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: critical
    annotations:
      summary: "Vault cluster has no active leader"
      description: "No Vault pod reports vault_core_active=1 for the past 5 minutes — Raft is stuck. Likely cause: TLS cluster cert mismatch after pod IP/addr drift. See docs/recovery/vault-cluster-cert-recovery.md."

  - alert: VaultPodSealed
    expr: vault_core_unsealed == 0
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: warning

Route critical via the existing ntfy-prod-critical receiver in alertmanager.

title: Auto-recover Vault no-leader / stale cluster-cert state in vault-unseal.yml
description:
On 2026-05-21 the Vault Raft cluster failed to elect a leader after a host reboot. Symptoms: all 3 pods unsealed and present in raft config, but inter-pod cluster RPC on port 8201 failed with `remote error: tls: unrecognized name`. Root cause was that the auto-generated cluster TLS cert (stored in encrypted Vault core data) had been issued against a `cluster_addr` value that no longer matched the pods' current `VAULT_CLUSTER_ADDR` env var. Only an active leader can regenerate that cert; no leader can be elected because the cert is broken. Chicken and egg.

Recovery required manual intervention:
1. Scale StatefulSet to 0
2. Spawn a temporary pod mounting all 3 vault PVCs
3. Wipe /vault/data on vault-raft-1 and vault-raft-2
4. Write a single-node peers.json on vault-raft-0 (only itself as voter)
5. Scale to 1, unseal vault-raft-0 → it bootstraps as a single-node cluster and elects itself leader, regenerating the cluster cert against current cluster_addr
6. Scale to 3; vault-raft-1 and vault-raft-2 boot empty, retry_join finds the leader, get a snapshot, unseal each → cluster healed

ansible/playbooks/maintenance/vault-unseal.yml currently does NOT detect this state. It tries to unseal followers, succeeds (sealed-state is unrelated), then fails at the "Login to Vault" task because the active service has no endpoints. The error is generic ("12 retries exhausted") and hides the underlying TLS issue.
design:
Add a new task block after "Assert all Vault pods are unsealed":

1. Poll for active leader: `kubectl exec ... vault status` and check `HA Mode=active`. Retry for ~60 seconds.
2. If no leader after polling AND pod logs show repeated `tls: unrecognized name` errors on port 8201, declare the cert-drift recovery condition.
3. Execute the documented recovery:
   - Scale StatefulSet to 0
   - Apply a recovery Pod manifest mounting all 3 data-vault-raft-N PVCs
   - Wipe vault-raft-1 and vault-raft-2 /vault/data
   - Write single-node peers.json on vault-raft-0 (selecting whichever node has the highest Raft index from the survey)
   - Scale to 1, wait for Running
   - Unseal vault-raft-0 with the keys from the vault-init secret
   - Wait for HA Mode=active
   - Scale to 3
   - Wait for vault-raft-1 and vault-raft-2 Running
   - Unseal each with the keys
   - Verify all 3 voters via `vault operator raft list-peers`
4. Make this opt-in via a tagged role (--tags vault-recover-cluster-cert) so the destructive recovery doesn't fire on a transient slow election.

Reference: docs/recovery/vault-cluster-cert-recovery.md (to be added) capturing the procedure prose for humans.
acceptance_criteria:
- Re-running vault-unseal.yml on a cluster in the cert-drift state automatically heals it without manual intervention.
- The playbook is idempotent — running it twice in a row with a healthy cluster is a no-op.
- A new runbook (docs/recovery/vault-cluster-cert-recovery.md) documents the procedure and the symptoms that trigger it.
- The argocd/apps/prod/vault.yaml uncommitted clusterAddr pin is committed as a complementary defense-in-depth fix.
notes:
2026-05-21 implementation committed in 7995103 + b79aef5:

1. argocd/apps/prod/vault.yaml — pinned server.ha.clusterAddr to "http://$(HOSTNAME).vault-raft-internal:8201" to prevent silent chart-template drift.

2. ansible/playbooks/maintenance/vault-unseal.yml — added detect+recover branch (~315 LOC inserted between "Assert all Vault pods are unsealed" and "Login to Vault"):
   - Waits up to ~90 s for a Raft leader on the primary pod
   - If no leader: greps recent logs for "tls: unrecognized name" cluster RPC errors
   - Default: fails with diagnostic message + exact re-run command
   - With -e vault_recover_cluster_cert=true: executes the documented recovery (scale to 0 → recovery pod mounts all PVCs → wipe followers → single-node peers.json on primary → scale to 1 + unseal + wait active → scale to full + unseal followers + verify list-peers)
   - Reuses existing vault_unseal_keys / vault_root_token facts; recovery branch is idempotent — re-running on a healthy cluster is a no-op

3. docs/recovery/vault-cluster-cert-recovery.md — new runbook with symptom, root cause, automated recovery command, and full manual fallback steps for debugging the automation itself.

Remaining work:
- Fire-drill the auto-recovery: re-induce the failure mode in a non-prod cluster and confirm the playbook heals it end-to-end without intervention. The actual code path has not yet been executed in anger — only the manual procedure it codifies has.
- Companion alert (home-infra-6qy) still to do, to catch the condition before someone notices via failing ExternalSecrets.

title: Provision tank/llm-models ZFS dataset and mount on GPU node
description:
Move LLM model storage off the ssd3 LV and onto a dedicated ZFS dataset on the `tank` HDD pool (14.5 TiB total, ~12.6 TiB free). LLM serving is read-only, sequential, and intermittent — a near-ideal fit for spinning disks + ZFS ARC. This also frees the upcoming SSD flash pool (formed from ssd2/ssd3 once the new SATA adapters are installed — see home-infra-sbd) for exclusive Longhorn use.

Cold load tradeoff: a 25 GiB Q6_K model takes ~2-3 min from HDD cold cache vs ~50 s from SATA SSD; after first load it lives in ARC at RAM speed. With llama-swap's 300 s TTL, swap-thrash will cost the cold load time but inference itself never touches disk.

User will redownload all 9 GGUFs (~205 GiB total) from Hugging Face into the new dataset.
design:
On atlas:
  zfs create -o recordsize=1M -o compression=lz4 -o atime=off tank/llm-models
  zfs set xattr=sa tank/llm-models

recordsize=1M improves sequential throughput for big GGUFs (default 128K is wasteful for files this size). compression=lz4 is essentially free; GGUFs barely compress but the codepath is fast. atime=off avoids spurious writes on read.

Expose to VM 107 (GPU node, k3s-prod-worker-gpu-1) via either:
  Option A — virtio-fs passthrough: faster (no NFS overhead), more setup. Add to VM config as `args: -object memory-backend-file...` etc, or use Proxmox's experimental virtiofs.
  Option B — NFS export from atlas: simpler, mature, decent throughput (~110-150 MB/s). atlas already serves other NFS to the VMs. Add to /etc/exports, mount in VM at /mnt/llm-models.

Recommendation: NFS for simplicity. The existing `argocd/manifests/llama-cpp/base/pv.yaml` is a local PV with nodeAffinity to k3s-prod-worker-gpu-1 and `local.path: /mnt/llm-models`. As long as that path exists in the VM (regardless of what backs it), the PV binds with zero IaC changes.

Final layout under /mnt/llm-models (mirrors prior ssd3 layout):
  GLM/                       — Z.ai GLM-4.7-Flash GGUFs (Q6_K + BF16 multi-shard)
  Qwopus3.5-9B-coder/        — community coder fine-tune
  gemma4/26B-A4B/, gemma4/31b/
  qwen3.6/27b/, qwen3.6/35b/ (3 quants)

Models can be reorganized after download — the PV doesn't care about internal layout, only the llama-swap ConfigMap's per-model paths need to match.
acceptance_criteria:
- ZFS dataset `tank/llm-models` exists on atlas with recordsize=1M, compression=lz4, atime=off
- VM 107 has `/mnt/llm-models` mounted (via NFS or virtio-fs) and the mount survives a reboot
- All 9 GGUFs from the model list (in issue comments / home-infra-0i6 design) are present under /mnt/llm-models
- `kubectl get pv llama-cpp-models-pv -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'` returns Available or Bound
- `bd close` once llama-swap can load at least one model from the new path
notes:
Implementation differs from original design (NFS export from atlas was overkill). User used the simpler block-device path:
- 600 GiB zvol `tank/vm-107-disk-2` attached to VM 107 as scsi2 (/dev/sdc)
- /dev/sdc1 formatted ext4
- Mounted at /mnt/llm-tank (fstab entry by UUID, nofail)
- Old /mnt/llm-models fstab entry (ssd3 LV) commented out

Remaining work:

title: Form new SSD flash pool from healthy drives + migrate Longhorn off tank
description:
The Samsung 870 EVO drives behind LVM VGs `ssd2` and `ssd3` became unavailable around 2026-05-19 due to a FAULTY SATA ADAPTER (not drive failure). Replacement adapters are scheduled to be installed 2026-05-21.

Original plan was to use ssd3 for LLM models; that workload is being moved to tank ZFS instead (see new sibling issue for `tank/llm-models`). Once the adapters are replaced and the drives are healthy, both ssd2 and ssd3 should be repurposed as a new flash storage pool dedicated to Longhorn replicas, replacing the current `general-storage`-tagged disks.

Goals after this:
- All Longhorn data lives on the new SSD pool (low-latency, high-IOPS)
- HDD-backed tank holds LLM models + bulk VM disks + media-adjacent storage
- Clean separation of workload classes by storage tier
design:
Steps once new SATA adapters are installed:
1. Verify both drives healthy: `smartctl -a /dev/sdX` on atlas; check for SATA link errors in dmesg
2. Decide pool topology: mirror (`zpool create flash mirror /dev/sd<X> /dev/sd<Y>`) for safety or stripe (single vdev) for capacity. Given Longhorn already replicates across nodes, a striped pool gives more usable space.
3. Create ZFS pool `flash` (or similar) on atlas with both drives
4. Add Longhorn `general-storage` tag to a new disk under each worker that has flash-backed storage
5. Drain replicas from the old LVM-backed disks; once empty, remove those disks from Longhorn
6. Update Ansible role `cluster_platform` so the new disk shows up automatically on worker provision

Affects: longhorn nodes config; possibly worker VM disk attach in `terraform/stacks/k3s/atlas/prod/workers`.
acceptance_criteria:
- New SATA adapters installed and both drives pass SMART/dmesg checks
- ZFS pool (or equivalent LVM VG) created on atlas using ssd2+ssd3
- New flash-backed disk attached to each cluster worker VM
- Longhorn shows the new disks tagged `general-storage` and healthy
- Old LVM-backed Longhorn disks drained and removed
- All currently-running Longhorn volumes have at least one replica on the new pool

title: Migrate Plex, Jellyfin, and Monitoring PVC to longhorn-redundant
description:
Three single-pod SQLite-backed apps (Grafana, Plex, Jellyfin) lacked application-layer HA and crashed hard during the 2026-05-19 ssd3 cascade when their Longhorn volumes went attached/faulted (not just attached/degraded). To raise resilience, a new `longhorn-redundant` StorageClass was added (numberOfReplicas:3, nodeSelector:general-storage, excludes the GPU worker which is I/O-stressed by transcoding + LLM workloads). Each PVC must be migrated to the new SC.

Because PVC `storageClassName` is immutable after binding, migration requires a new PVC under a transient name (`<old-pvc>-rdn`) + an rsync data copy + a deployment claimName swap.
design:
Per-app procedure (~30 min per small app, ~5 h for Jellyfin's 58 GiB at observed 3-4 MB/s):
1. Annotate source Longhorn volume with `longhorn.io/take-snapshot=pre-rdn-migration` (NFS backup safety net).
2. Disable ArgoCD self-heal on the app's Application (so manual scale-to-0 isn't reverted).
3. `kubectl scale deployment $APP --replicas=0` and wait for pods gone.
4. Create new PVC `<old>-rdn` with `storageClassName: longhorn-redundant`.
5. Apply an alpine + rsync sidecar pod mounting both PVCs at /src and /dst; `rsync -aHAX --info=progress2 /src/ /dst/`.
6. Wait for Succeeded; verify `du -sh /src /dst` matches.
7. Update IaC: rename PVC in `base/pvc.yaml`, switch `claimName` in `base/deployment.yaml`, remove any prod overlay PVC patches.
8. Commit + push; ArgoCD reconciles with the app's self-heal re-enabled.
9. Delete migration pod, old PVC, old static PV, and the orphan Longhorn volume.

Reference docs/runbook: `argocd/manifests/longhorn-redundant-sc/README.md`.
acceptance_criteria:
- All three PVCs (`kube-prometheus-stack-grafana-rdn`, `plex-config-pvc-rdn`, `jellyfin-config-pvc-rdn`) bound on `longhorn-redundant` SC with 3 replicas across general-storage nodes
- Old static PVs (`plex-config-pv`, `jellyfin-config-pv`) and their Longhorn source volumes deleted
- Live-patch comment blocks removed from `argocd/manifests/jellyfin/base/pvc.yaml` (the Plex one was cleared during its migration)
- ArgoCD `root-prod` and `jellyfin` Applications have self-heal re-enabled (currently disabled for the migration)

title: Use ESP32 onboard blue LED as car-telemetry connection status light
description:
Drive the ESP32 dev board's onboard blue LED (GPIO2 on esp32dev) as a status indicator so device state is visible without serial or the HUD.

Suggested patterns (non-blocking, millis()-driven, no delay()):
- Off: no power / firmware not running (a hang is visible as a frozen pattern)
- Slow blink: booted, no Wi-Fi STA connection (AP only)
- Double blink: BLE OBD dongle not connected
- Solid: Wi-Fi + BLE connected
- Fast flicker: upload in progress; brief long pulse on upload failure

Context: 2026-09-25 device went silent after f783de4 (scan-and-join Wi-Fi) with no way to tell hang vs no-Wi-Fi vs no-power in the car. Acceptance: pattern table documented in firmware README; states verified on the bench by toggling Wi-Fi/BLE.

title: Stale pve1 (172.20.20.11) in NetBox and ansible lxc defaults
description:
NetBox has a device 'pve1' at 172.20.20.11 with dns_name pve1.levangie.org, but it is not a member of the 'oasis' Proxmox cluster (pvecm nodes shows only atlas, elitedesk-1, dellssf) and it does not respond to ping.

It is also still referenced as the default LXC target in three places:
  ansible/group_vars/lxc.yml:6          lxc_default_node: pve1
  ansible/roles/lxc/defaults/main.yml:11 lxc_default_node: pve1
  ansible/lxc_definitions/containers/nbn-srv.yml:11  node: pve1
  ansible/inventories/lxc/hosts.yml:26  pve1:

So deploying an LXC with the default node would target a host that no longer exists. This is pre-existing dead configuration, not caused by the 2.5G re-network work.

Needs a decision on whether pve1 is genuinely retired, then a coordinated cleanup across NetBox, its DNS record, and the ansible defaults - which should point at a real node instead.
acceptance_criteria: pve1 confirmed retired or restored; if retired, removed from NetBox and the ansible lxc defaults repointed to a live Proxmox node.
notes:
2026-08-14: user confirmed pve1/pve2/pve3 are all retired and atlas is the primary node. Resolved the ansible side:
  ansible/group_vars/lxc.yml            lxc_default_node: pve1 -> atlas
  ansible/roles/lxc/defaults/main.yml   lxc_default_node: pve1 -> atlas
  ansible/lxc_definitions/containers/nbn-srv.yml  node: pve1 -> atlas (CT 200 is not deployed on any host, so nothing moved)
  ansible/inventories/lxc/hosts.yml     removed the pve1 entry
Both values verified resolving to 'atlas' via ansible -m debug.

NetBox pve1 set to status=decommissioning rather than deleted, so the 172.20.20.11 reservation stays visible. Its DNS record pve1.levangie.org is manually managed in Technitium (the sync logs it as 'not netbox-sync managed'), so NetBox changes do not affect it - removing that record is a separate manual step.

STILL OPEN: terraform/stacks/k3s/compact-3node/prod/main.tf:78 has default = ["pve1", "pve2", "pve3"]. That is the legacy compact-3node stack with no local state; left alone as out of scope. The terraform/archive/ copies are archived and can stay.
close_reason: Ansible LXC defaults repointed from the retired pve1 to atlas across all four files and verified. NetBox pve1 marked decommissioning. Remaining pve1/pve2/pve3 references are confined to the legacy compact-3node terraform stack and terraform/archive/, both out of scope and recorded in the notes.

Left deliberately unchanged: netbox-technitium-sync pushes dns_name straight into the levangie.org zone, so editing it would delete one DNS record and create another. That is an outward-facing change and needs a decision, not a silent fix.

Nothing functional in home-infra depends on the hostname - terraform/stacks/k3s/dellssf/prod/control-plane/main.tf uses the IP 172.20.20.14 directly, and the only other hits are code comments. Risk is limited to bookmarks, external configs, and anything outside this repo.

close_reason: Renamed 2026-08-14 per the user's convention: DNS name matches the Proxmox node name. Added A dellssf.levangie.org -> 172.20.20.14, deleted the old A, and left dell-sff.levangie.org as a CNAME to dellssf.levangie.org as a transition alias (both still resolve to .14, so nothing can break; the alias is safe to delete once confirmed unused). NetBox dns_name updated to match. Verified nothing in the repo, cluster configmaps/secrets, Prometheus scrape targets or the Caddy config referenced the old name - Prometheus already targets 172.20.20.14 with label proxmox_host=dellssf.

title: Decide on Proxmox migration: type=insecure
description:
/etc/pve/datacenter.cfg has no migration: key, so Proxmox defaults to 'secure' and tunnels the migration stream over SSH. On dellssf (i3-8100T, 4 threads) that encryption - not the wire - is the bottleneck, so a 2.5G link will go largely unused for migrations.

Setting 'migration: type=insecure,network=172.20.20.0/22' typically gives 2-3x faster migration but sends VM memory and disk UNENCRYPTED over the LAN.

USER DECISION REQUIRED - this is a security tradeoff, not a technical one. Reasonable on a trusted flat home LAN, but it is the user's call.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit go/no-go recorded. If yes, datacenter.cfg updated and a timed qm migrate compared before/after.
close_reason: User approved insecure migration on the trusted LAN. Applied 2026-08-14: added 'migration: type=insecure,network=172.20.20.0/22' to /etc/pve/datacenter.cfg on atlas; verified propagated to elitedesk-1 and dellssf via /etc/pve cluster sync, and parsed by the API as {'network': '172.20.20.0/22', 'type': 'insecure'}. Backup of the original saved to /root/datacenter.cfg.bak-2026-08-14 on atlas. Timed before/after migration comparison still pending the 2.5G cabling.

title: Document 2.5G topology + bond runbook in docs/operations
description:
The bond config is deliberately NOT automated in Ansible (one-time change on three hosts; a bad rewrite of /etc/network/interfaces makes a host unreachable with no remote rollback - AGENTS.md rule 2, no abstraction for single-use code).

So the repo needs a written record instead: the port map for both switches, the three final /etc/network/interfaces files, and the per-host change procedure including the failover test.
acceptance_criteria: docs/operations/ contains a network topology + bond runbook covering both switches' port assignments, all three host configs, and the verification steps.
close_reason: docs/operations/network-topology.md added in c69d68d2 and indexed from docs/README.md. Covers both switch port maps, the three host bond configs, the per-host change procedure with failover test, the 1GbE baseline, NAS LAG throughput model, and the design decisions (no jumbo frames, no Multus storage network, not Ansible-automated).

title: Cable + bond atlas (last, biggest capacity hit)
description:
atlas nic0 is already at 2500Mb/s on the 2.5G switch, so this task is only about adding the standby leg: cable unused onboard nic1 to the 1G switch and convert vmbr0 onto an active-backup bond0.

Lower value than the other two (atlas's 2.5G is onboard and reliable, not USB) but it costs only a free 1G switch port and buys a rescue path if nic0 or its switch port fails.

Do this LAST: atlas hosts cp-1 plus all four workers, so it is the biggest capacity hit.
